project.name: Pytyliki Processor IDE
project.purpose: A unified processor and microarchitecture engineering IDE for target-aware development, assembly and IR inspection, register/memory/pipeline visualization, simulation, debugging, measurement, verification and hardware qualification.

baseline.current_product_boundary: The audited main branch contains a C11 processor workstation, read-only CPU/usable-ISA discovery, bounded benchmarks, a 20-entry enhancement/workspace registry, memory and trace primitives, reference embedded models, and a capability-gated low-level target/memory/RAM-MMIO/clock-power/IRQ contract tested with a fake backend. It does not yet ship a unified Processor IDE with live register panes, assembly editor/disassembler, pipeline/cycle simulator, physical logic-analyzer transport or vendor debug integration.

ownership.pytyliki: Owns the IDE shell, project/target model, processor workspace registry, native processor APIs, simulator orchestration, debug/provider adapters, traces, diagnostics and qualification reports.
ownership.reaper: Owns canonical source-language grammar, type/effect semantics, Span/SourceMap, typed IR, compiler passes and shared ABI contracts. Processor IDE consumes these; it does not implement a competing language parser or IR.
ownership.duck_os: Mediates privileged device access, process isolation, drivers, memory mapping, interrupt routing, debug permissions and local hardware services.
ownership.board_and_vendor_backends: Provide board/SoC/CPU stepping profiles, register maps, debug transports, timing/power data, errata and laboratory instrument adapters with provenance.

system_workspace_registry.reuse_policy: Reuse the existing twenty named enhancement domains as the Processor IDE's top-level workspace taxonomy. They are workspace groups in one IDE, not twenty separate applications, hardware privilege levels or independent control planes.

native_session_foundation.description: Initial C11 target-aware session API that reuses the existing 20-workspace registry and pl_ll_target descriptor. It validates inspect/plan/static/simulate/debug/HIL/privileged preflight declarations only. Session flags are not security tokens or hardware grants; every actual operation must still pass pl_ll_bus capability checks and trusted OS/board backend authorization. The API itself performs no device access or hardware mutation.

panes.purpose: Project, target, ISA/ABI, stepping, board, OS and execution-mode identity.
Source editor, Reaper typed IR, spans, diagnostics and source-to-machine navigation.
Assembler, disassembler, bytes, symbols, relocations, sections and memory map.
Target-specific architectural registers, flags, access class and before/after diff.
Virtual/physical/bus/MMIO address spaces, pages, regions, permissions and DMA ownership.
Model-dependent stages, queues, stalls, hazards, predictor, issue and retirement timeline.
Clock domains, waveforms, cycle/timing/latency evidence, power and thermal signals.
Bounded event capture, breakpoints, checkpoints, replay and divergence analysis.
Reproducible build graph, target matrix, golden tests, CI and artifact verification.
Source-mapped diagnostics, register/memory/trace/project diffs and remediation.

shell.selection_rule: All panes bind to the same project, target profile, execution mode and evidence context; each pane may show a different abstraction but may not silently switch target identity.

target_model.unknown_policy: Unknown target fields remain explicitly unknown; no default assumption about endian, register names, cache line, instruction width or privilege model.

modes.description: Read-only host/target metadata and existing evidence.
Inert build, debug, target or lab operation plans.
Parsing, type/effect analysis, lint and artifact inspection.
Execution against a named CPU/device/circuit model.
Debug sessions with explicit halt/read/write side effects and permission.
Named physical target tests under a documented lab/board procedure.
Narrow OS/driver-mediated access to privileged CPU or device operations.

invariants: Live, simulated, estimated, fixture and unknown values are visually and structurally distinct.
A UI refresh rate is not a hardware sampling rate.
TSC ticks, core cycles, device ticks and wall-clock time are separate units unless a calibrated mapping is supplied.
Unbuffered sampling is not a prerequisite; bounded capture buffers report overflow and dropped events.
A CPU profile, instruction catalogue or model cannot certify an untested physical target.
A debugger or probe may perturb, halt or change target execution; its effect is recorded.
Hardware observations, architectural documentation and errata are compared rather than silently treating one as infallible.

rule_status_legend.partial: A supporting primitive exists in main, but the integrated Processor IDE behavior is not shipped.
rule_status_legend.planned: A concrete IDE requirement with an acceptance condition; no integrated implementation is claimed.
rule_status_legend.research: Requires validated microarchitecture, analog, physical-design or external laboratory models/tooling.

rules.title: Target-bound project entry
rules.requirement: Open a project with an explicit target profile, ISA, ABI, silicon/board revision when known, OS/runtime context and selected execution mode.
rules.acceptance: A project cannot start a build or target session with an unresolved target; unknown fields remain unknown and are never guessed.

rules.title: Signal and phase workspace
rules.requirement: Display signal transitions, trace timestamps, sample cadence, measured latency and uncertainty for the selected model or instrumented target.
rules.acceptance: Each plotted series identifies live, simulated, estimated or unknown provenance, sampling method, clock source and dropped-sample count.
rules.interpretation_adjustment: Do not promise unbuffered display or a universal 1 ns UI response; preserve bounded capture and report measurement/display latency.

rules.title: Versioned machine platform description
rules.requirement: Keep register maps, memory regions, buses, interrupt vectors, clock domains, timing constraints and feature gates in one versioned target description.
rules.acceptance: Schema validation rejects overlaps, invalid widths, impossible alignments and incompatible target revisions.

rules.title: Direct tool integration without hidden layers
rules.requirement: Connect assembler, compiler, simulator, trace analyzer and code generator through explicit versioned contracts and visible data transformations.
rules.acceptance: Every adapter declares input/output schema, version, failure mode, provenance and resource limits; no hidden background operation occurs.

rules.title: Reproducible native build infrastructure
rules.requirement: Build target images, symbol tables, descriptor tables and map files from pinned, inspectable inputs.
rules.acceptance: Repeated builds from pinned inputs are byte-identical except for documented non-deterministic fields; output includes toolchain and target metadata.

rules.title: Assembly-first machine view
rules.requirement: Allow direct inspection and editing of target assembly/machine code while preserving source, IR, symbol, Span and ABI context.
rules.acceptance: A selected instruction can be traced to its source/IR origin when available and to its address/encoding in the target image.
rules.interpretation_adjustment: Assembly-first does not ban Reaper, C, HDL or other declared source layers; it exposes explicit lowering rather than hiding it.

rules.title: Unified processor execution timeline
rules.requirement: Synchronize simulator state, pipeline, cache/TLB, memory, interrupts and events into a single logical timeline.
rules.acceptance: A simulation step updates all modeled components atomically; live hardware streams use timestamp correlation and declare skew rather than pretending all devices share one clock.

rules.title: Microprocessor execution context
rules.requirement: Show active target mode, privilege, execution context, core/thread, clock domain, memory permissions and capabilities at the selected node.
rules.acceptance: The context panel shows unknown/unavailable separately from false/disabled and displays the provider of every detected field.

rules.title: Live and simulated register inspector
rules.requirement: Display the target's documented architectural register set, aliases and flags, including R0–R7 when defined, PC, FLAGS and the project-defined regit view when explicitly declared.
rules.acceptance: Register names, widths, access classes and read/write effects derive from the selected ISA/target descriptor. regit is shown only as a declared project/debugger view, never fabricated as a universal architectural register; changed values are diffed per trace event.
rules.interpretation_adjustment: Do not invent universal registers such as regit or assume all architectures expose R0-R7; hardware watch may be sampled or disruptive.

rules.title: Bit-level construction interface
rules.requirement: Provide exact bit/field views for masks, slices, shifts, rotates, sign extension, overflow and descriptor layouts.
rules.acceptance: Round-trip tests prove bit offsets, widths and endian interpretation against target fixtures; dangerous truncation is surfaced before emission.

rules.title: Instruction workbench
rules.requirement: Correlate source line, typed IR operation, assembly mnemonic, encoded bytes, decoded operands, target feature requirements and available cost evidence.
rules.acceptance: A selected instruction shows origin, exact encoding and whether cost is static estimate, simulator result or live measurement.
rules.interpretation_adjustment: Cycle costs must be target/model-specific and cannot be inferred universally from mnemonic alone.

rules.title: Typed address execution map
rules.requirement: Visualize virtual, physical, bus, I/O-port and MMIO addresses with page boundaries, permissions, alignment and mappings.
rules.acceptance: Address-space types cannot be mixed implicitly; every live physical/device map comes from a capability-gated target provider.

rules.title: Microarchitecture profile library
rules.requirement: Store versioned reference profiles for pipeline stages, branch prediction, queues, execution units, cache hierarchy and retirement policy.
rules.acceptance: Every profile identifies source/revision, scope, assumptions and modeled features; custom models pass schema and conformance tests.

rules.title: Scenario execution platform
rules.requirement: Run programs against reference CPU/device models, instruction emulators and declared hardware fixtures before any target session.
rules.acceptance: The result includes simulator version, model identity, seed, supported-instruction coverage and divergence from expected fixtures.

rules.title: Privilege and reset verification
rules.requirement: Check boot/reset entry, privilege transitions, interrupt vectors, protected regions and OS-mediated capabilities against the selected target.
rules.acceptance: Negative tests prove unprivileged actions cannot reach privileged callbacks; reset/boot claims require a board or emulator backend.

rules.title: Snapshot and before/after comparison
rules.requirement: Capture and diff register state, flags, memory ranges, pipeline model state and relevant device-model state before and after an operation.
rules.acceptance: Snapshots identify captured fields and omitted state; diffs are deterministic and respect permissions and sensitive-memory policies.

rules.title: Core activity and synchronization monitor
rules.requirement: Inspect core/thread load, queue occupancy, locks, barriers, waits and memory-order events where providers expose them.
rules.acceptance: Every metric identifies sample interval and scope; simulated and OS-observed data are never mixed.

rules.title: Digital logic and FSM workbench
rules.requirement: Model Boolean logic, sequential elements, finite-state machines, truth tables, state reachability and transition conditions.
rules.acceptance: Exhaustive small-state tests or bounded model checks identify unreachable states, dead ends and invalid transitions.

rules.title: Hardware dependency map
rules.requirement: Mark instructions, registers, timing assumptions, MMIO layouts and bus behavior tied to specific silicon, stepping or board revisions.
rules.acceptance: A target incompatibility is reported before build/launch; portable paths and unsupported target-specific paths are visibly separated.

rules.title: No-hidden-runtime execution profile
rules.requirement: Provide explicit no_alloc, no_std/bare-metal and bounded-runtime build profiles for critical code and target artifacts.
rules.acceptance: The build report lists runtime, allocator, TLS, exception, dynamic-loader and background-service dependencies; each profile fails closed on disallowed dependencies.
rules.interpretation_adjustment: No-runtime is an opt-in target profile, not a blanket ban on useful IDE/runtime features.

rules.title: Measured and estimated operation cost
rules.requirement: Show cycles, latency, memory traffic and energy costs before simulation where static target data exists, then compare against execution evidence.
rules.acceptance: Each value is labeled measured, estimated, simulated or unknown and includes units, target, method and uncertainty.

rules.title: Explicit narrowing and signedness
rules.requirement: Require visible casts for narrowing, signedness changes, pointer-width conversions and truncating bitfields.
rules.acceptance: Static diagnostics flag potential value loss and provide boundary tests for accepted conversions.

rules.title: Alignment checking
rules.requirement: Validate alignment for buffers, page tables, instruction fetch, descriptor rings and target structures.
rules.acceptance: The diagnostic states required and actual alignment and distinguishes architecturally faulting accesses from merely slower ones.

rules.title: FSM reachability and deadlock checks
rules.requirement: Analyze state-machine reachability, terminal states, deadlocks and event-triggered transition completeness.
rules.acceptance: A bounded or formal check produces a counterexample trace for each detected deadlock or unreachable state.

rules.title: Clock-domain crossing contracts
rules.requirement: Require explicit synchronizers, async FIFOs or documented CDC bridges between unrelated clock domains.
rules.acceptance: CDC lint rejects unbridged crossings and records synchronizer depth, reset behavior and metastability assumptions.

rules.title: Energy and time windows
rules.requirement: Validate declared timing and energy budgets such as within_window<N> and energy_cap<E> against measured or modeled data.
rules.acceptance: The run fails or reports indeterminate when a required budget is exceeded or the evidence is insufficient; units and tolerances are explicit.

rules.title: Constant-time security inspection
rules.requirement: Warn about secret-dependent branches, memory addresses, lookup tables and variable-latency operations inside constant-time regions.
rules.acceptance: Static findings and target-specific timing tests are reported as risk evidence, not as a proof of universal side-channel absence.

rules.title: Stable diagnostic status vocabulary
rules.requirement: Use stable machine-readable codes for parse/type/ABI/permission/timeout/overflow/device/simulation failures.
rules.acceptance: Every error has a code, severity, source span or target location, remediation and stable serialization.

rules.title: Named constants and physical units
rules.requirement: Require named constants for masks, slot addresses, thresholds and timing/power/energy quantities with explicit units.
rules.acceptance: Lint identifies raw numeric literals in policy-sensitive contexts; values use unit-safe types or documented suffixes such as _cyc, _bytes and _pj.

rules.title: Readable control-flow assistance
rules.requirement: Offer refactor suggestions for excessive nesting, duplicated predicates and unclear early-exit structure.
rules.acceptance: Suggestions preserve semantics, show a diff and require user acceptance; no silent source rewrite occurs.

rules.title: Deterministic crash reproduction
rules.requirement: Record input, instruction position, target/model revision, register checkpoint and event ordering for replayable failures.
rules.acceptance: Replay reproduces the same modeled state or identifies the first divergence; live-hardware nondeterminism is explicitly captured as evidence rather than claimed deterministic.

rules.title: Precise before/after diff
rules.requirement: Compare register, memory, flags, device model, build artifacts and pull-request changes by named ranges and provenance.
rules.acceptance: Diffs identify changed fields and omitted/unreadable regions; secret data is redacted by policy.

rules.title: Dead-code and dead-state analysis
rules.requirement: Detect unreachable labels, unused registers, unreferenced symbols, dead flags and unreachable basic blocks where target semantics permit.
rules.acceptance: Findings are source-mapped and architecture-aware; special-register side effects and inline assembly clobbers prevent unsafe false positives.

rules.title: Safe rollback and recovery
rules.requirement: Record failure points and restore only supported logical snapshots, simulator state or version-controlled artifacts.
rules.acceptance: Rollback reports restored and non-restorable state; it never implies reversal of external device or physical events.

rules.title: No hidden IDE side effects
rules.requirement: Autocomplete, navigation, analysis and suggested actions must remain observational until the user explicitly runs a command.
rules.acceptance: Tests prove editor suggestions do not launch tools, change devices, write MMIO, install drivers or alter target state.

rules.title: Canonical operation forms
rules.requirement: Prefer one canonical spelling/API per operation while keeping explicit aliases where compatibility or ISA syntax requires them.
rules.acceptance: Aliases normalize to one stable semantic ID and preserve original source spans for diagnostics.

rules.title: Positive state names
rules.requirement: Prefer positive names such as is_ready, is_locked and is_valid in new APIs and generated examples.
rules.acceptance: Lint detects confusing double negatives in new declarations without renaming externally specified ISA symbols.

rules.title: Intent-first comments
rules.requirement: Explain why an implementation choice exists and which hardware/toolchain limitation it respects.
rules.acceptance: Documentation review flags comments that merely restate code; public hardware assumptions are documented.

rules.title: Novice-readable onboarding
rules.requirement: Provide guided target setup, project tour, register/trace explanations and working examples for the main IDE screens.
rules.acceptance: A new user can open a sample target project, run a safe simulation and inspect a trace using only in-product guidance.

rules.title: Fast feedback loop
rules.requirement: Keep edit, syntax/type checks, contract validation, incremental build and trace inspection responsive through caching and incremental work.
rules.acceptance: CI records timings for each stage; local performance budgets are target-class-specific rather than a universal seconds guarantee.

rules.title: Small, reviewable PR flow
rules.requirement: Generate focused change sets with a clear acceptance criterion and independent tests for each subsystem.
rules.acceptance: A PR checklist identifies affected contracts, target profiles, tests, docs, migrations and downstream repositories.

rules.title: Sequential integration into main
rules.requirement: Rebase/update each next integration PR against the latest accepted mainline and honor branch protection/rulesets.
rules.acceptance: Merge automation refuses stale base commits, failed required checks, unresolved conflicts and dependency-order violations.

rules.title: Automatic validation pipeline
rules.requirement: Run format/lint, unit tests, schema validation, simulator golden tests, sanitizers and target-specific checks on relevant changes.
rules.acceptance: CI reports each gate separately and cannot pass a hardware gate using only a host fixture.

rules.title: Unified engineering metrics
rules.requirement: Normalize cycles, instruction count, code size, cache events, stalls, tests, coverage, energy and thermal measurements across modules.
rules.acceptance: Metric records include unit, target, evidence mode, provider, context and uncertainty; incompatible samples cannot be compared.

rules.title: External toolchain interoperability
rules.requirement: Integrate C/ASM, linker/debugger, HDL, waveform, EDA and vendor tools through declared adapters and versioned artifacts.
rules.acceptance: Tool support matrix distinguishes installed, detected, validated, invoked and fully integrated states.

rules.title: Compact core and opt-in extensions
rules.requirement: Keep the IDE shell and core contracts small; load experimental target packs, EDA tools and debug adapters explicitly.
rules.acceptance: Extension manifests declare permissions, ABI, target support and dependencies; unknown extensions are rejected safely.

rules.title: Fast navigation and keyboard workflow
rules.requirement: Provide command palette, symbol search, register search, go-to-definition, history and configurable hotkeys.
rules.acceptance: UI interaction latency is benchmarked on named reference machines and large projects; no instant-response guarantee is assumed.

rules.title: Hot-path and resource profiler
rules.requirement: Rank expensive instructions, pipeline waits, memory stalls, cache events and power/thermal costs from available evidence.
rules.acceptance: Profiles distinguish actual counters, simulator estimates and sampling bias, and identify profiler overhead.

rules.title: Workspace lifecycle and deprecation
rules.requirement: Retire obsolete panels, rules and adapters through versioned migration notes while preserving old project readability.
rules.acceptance: Deprecated features carry removal versions and migration paths; no accepted project is silently reinterpreted.

rules.title: Backward-compatible evolution
rules.requirement: Version project formats, target descriptions, plugins, AST/IR interchange and trace formats with explicit migration policy.
rules.acceptance: Golden fixtures prove supported prior versions remain readable or receive an explicit migration diagnostic.

rules.title: Assembly-first, not abstraction-blind
rules.requirement: The default machine view leads with decoded instructions and registers, while retaining source, Reaper IR, C, HDL and model layers as explicit navigable levels.
rules.acceptance: Every supported source layer has a visible lowering path; target assembly and machine bytes are inspectable for built artifacts.
rules.interpretation_adjustment: Reject the blanket ban on all languages above ASM: the IDE must expose abstractions without hiding or forbidding them.

rules.title: Instrumented bus timeline
rules.requirement: Display sampled bus transactions and logic signals from a simulator or explicitly instrumented target with timestamps and capture metadata.
rules.acceptance: The UI declares sample rate, buffer depth, trigger, drop count, transport delay and probe intrusion; no universal 1 ns UI deadline is claimed.
rules.interpretation_adjustment: Use bounded capture buffers for reliability; distinguish hardware event time from UI render latency.

rules.title: Voltage and signal-state palette
rules.requirement: Provide a signal-specific legend for VCC/high, GND/low, floating, contended, unknown and high-impedance states.
rules.acceptance: Color is redundant with labels/patterns and meets contrast/accessibility checks; palette is configurable per project.
rules.interpretation_adjustment: Do not conflate voltage colors with the global editor/status palette; electrical states need more than three colors.

rules.title: Versioned physical layout artifacts
rules.requirement: Treat floorplan, placement, routing, pin map, constraints and cell/library references as versioned project artifacts.
rules.acceptance: Every layout artifact references process/library version, die revision, units, source RTL/netlist digest and tool provenance.

rules.title: Area and utilization analysis
rules.requirement: Measure cell area, macro area, density, congestion, whitespace, timing and power for a declared process/library.
rules.acceptance: Reports distinguish utilization and routability constraints; empty area is not filled with arbitrary structures.
rules.interpretation_adjustment: Reject automatic insertion of noise structures to fill all whitespace; floorplanning must satisfy DRC/timing/thermal constraints.

rules.title: Thermal and power prediction
rules.requirement: Estimate thermal hotspots from a validated power map, package/cooling model and boundary conditions; compare with available sensors.
rules.acceptance: Predictions include model, calibration, time horizon, uncertainty and safety margin; target writes remain capability-gated.
rules.interpretation_adjustment: A prediction cannot guarantee warning before damage without validated sensors and conservative limits.

rules.title: Clocked and asynchronous domains
rules.requirement: Model synchronous domains by declared clock edges and asynchronous crossings through explicit CDC primitives.
rules.acceptance: CDC checks validate synchronizers, reset crossings and handshake/FIFO protocols; asynchronous subsystems are not forced into one global clock.

rules.title: Pipeline hazard and stall accounting
rules.requirement: Represent stalls, bubbles, replay, flushes and hazard reasons in the selected pipeline model and trace.
rules.acceptance: Every modeled stall has an explicit cause and cycle interval; optimizer changes preserve architectural behavior and the model's constraints.
rules.interpretation_adjustment: Never delete a required stall or hazard to satisfy a cosmetic no-bubble rule.

rules.title: Target-specific branch prediction policy
rules.requirement: Describe predictor profile, branch hints and history behavior per ISA/microarchitecture.
rules.acceptance: Static hints are explicit and benchmarked; unsupported hints are rejected or ignored only under documented target rules.
rules.interpretation_adjustment: Do not assume every branch is taken by default; predictor behavior varies by core and workload.

rules.title: Silicon stepping compatibility
rules.requirement: Bind images and target operations to compatible silicon stepping, board revision, errata and feature sets.
rules.acceptance: An incompatible revision is blocked; compatible revisions follow an explicit tested compatibility matrix.

rules.title: Glitch and fault artifact capture
rules.requirement: Capture glitches, malformed waveforms, transient model states and fault-injection cases as reproducible test artifacts.
rules.acceptance: Artifacts include model/target, trigger, capture window, seed, expected/observed state and recovery outcome.
rules.interpretation_adjustment: A glitch is a diagnostic/fault artifact, not accepted corrupted production state.

rules.title: Failure-analysis export
rules.requirement: Export crash bundles, traces, waveform windows, register snapshots, netlists and metadata for external failure-analysis tools/labs.
rules.acceptance: Exports use documented formats and redact secrets; microscope/FA equipment is never automatically controlled by a crash handler.

rules.title: Source as canonical; binary as derived artifact
rules.requirement: Keep human-readable source, declarative hardware models and versioned binary outputs linked through digests and reproducible build metadata.
rules.acceptance: A clean checkout can rebuild artifacts and verify source-to-binary provenance.
rules.interpretation_adjustment: Reject binary-only source-of-truth storage; preserve inspectable and reviewable source.

rules.title: Static or monolithic image profiles
rules.requirement: Offer fully static/monolithic bare-metal images where target requirements demand them while allowing dynamic linking when ABI and runtime policy permit.
rules.acceptance: Build report lists every linked module, relocation, runtime dependency, load region and reproducibility input.
rules.interpretation_adjustment: Dynamic libraries are not inherently nondeterministic; policy is target/profile-specific.

rules.title: Hardware-backed key and entropy providers
rules.requirement: Use approved entropy sources and platform key providers such as TPM/secure elements where available; keep keys opaque to the IDE.
rules.acceptance: Randomness health tests and key-provider provenance are explicit; secrets are not derived from an assumed CPU noise source.
rules.interpretation_adjustment: Do not encrypt all code by default or claim CPU noise is a secure key generator without validated entropy conditioning.

rules.title: Canonical ISA mnemonic registry
rules.requirement: Expose each target ISA's canonical instruction names, encoding, aliases and disassembly spelling in a versioned registry.
rules.acceptance: Aliases normalize to canonical semantic IDs while preserving source spelling and assembler compatibility.
rules.interpretation_adjustment: Do not force MOV/LOAD/STORE names across unrelated ISAs or delete valid architectural aliases.

rules.title: Register change and dirty-state visualization
rules.requirement: Highlight registers changed by a selected instruction/event and distinguish dirty compiler values, architectural writes and debugger modifications.
rules.acceptance: Diff markers are tied to trace sequence and access provenance; animation can be disabled and is not the only indicator.

rules.title: Typed condition flags
rules.requirement: Model target flags such as zero, carry, overflow, sign and interrupt state as typed architecture-specific state.
rules.acceptance: Flag reads/writes and preservation are validated from instruction metadata and calling-convention rules.
rules.interpretation_adjustment: Flags can be represented in APIs where the target ABI permits; they are not forced into ordinary function parameters.

rules.title: Interrupt priority and affinity policy
rules.requirement: Model interrupt routing, priority, affinity, masking, nesting and coalescing according to the target interrupt controller.
rules.acceptance: No interrupt is silently dropped; coalescing is allowed only for declared edge/level semantics and documented loss policy.

rules.title: Atomic operation semantics
rules.requirement: Describe atomicity, width, memory order, lock-free guarantees and bus/device scope per ISA and target.
rules.acceptance: Litmus tests and target fixtures verify compare-exchange/RMW ordering; unavailable widths or semantics fail explicitly.
rules.interpretation_adjustment: Do not require every RMW to take one cycle or globally lock a bus; hardware guarantees are architecture-specific.

rules.title: Inter-core coherency and communication
rules.requirement: Model cache coherence, shared memory ordering, message passing, barriers and synchronization channels across cores.
rules.acceptance: Concurrency tests validate visibility and race freedom under the selected memory model; coherence capabilities are target-specific.

rules.title: Micro-operation and microcode inspection
rules.requirement: Expose uop decomposition and microcode metadata only when documented or provided by a supported softcore/vendor tool.
rules.acceptance: A view records source/provenance and separates observed uops from inferred decomposition.
rules.interpretation_adjustment: Do not promise arbitrary microcode editing on commercial CPUs; edits require a supported programmable core and vendor contract.

rules.title: Cache-line and transfer geometry
rules.requirement: Use target-described cache-line size, burst length, sector size and memory transfer granularity for visualization and warnings.
rules.acceptance: Alignment and efficiency warnings derive from target profile and measured data; byte-granular valid operations remain valid.
rules.interpretation_adjustment: Never hard-code 64 bytes as a universal cache line or call every sub-line access inefficient.

rules.title: TLB invalidation and shootdown model
rules.requirement: Describe address-space invalidation scope, required barriers, interprocessor notifications and completion acknowledgements per architecture/OS.
rules.acceptance: Model or target adapter verifies required ordering and completion before affected mappings are reused.

rules.title: Architectural register names and semantic aliases
rules.requirement: Retain canonical ISA register names while allowing contextual aliases such as ACCUMULATOR or INDEX_PTR in source/debug views.
rules.acceptance: Aliases resolve to a canonical register identity and never obscure width, role or ABI constraints.
rules.interpretation_adjustment: Do not rename architectural registers based only on local variable roles.

rules.title: Context save/restore and ABI volatility
rules.requirement: Generate save/restore sets from ABI caller/callee-saved rules, interrupt frames, vector state and target context requirements.
rules.acceptance: Conformance tests verify preserved state across calls, interrupts and context switches for each target ABI.
rules.interpretation_adjustment: Do not assume only a generic minimal register set is saved; lazy vector state and nested interrupts change the contract.

rules.title: Privileged register access policy
rules.requirement: Gate MSR/control/debug register access by ISA privilege state, OS permission, target capability and backend support.
rules.acceptance: Denied accesses fail before backend invocation; policy accounts for x86 rings, ARM exception levels, RISC-V privilege modes and other targets.

rules.title: Bit-shift and carry semantics
rules.requirement: Expose whether shifts/rotates produce carry/overflow flags and how lost bits are represented according to the target ISA.
rules.acceptance: Instruction-level tests cover each shift width, count boundary and target flag result.
rules.interpretation_adjustment: A discarded bit is not automatically a data leak; flags and results follow ISA-defined semantics.

rules.title: Masking and branch trade-off analysis
rules.requirement: Offer bitmask lowering as an optimization candidate when it is semantically correct and improves the target cost/security profile.
rules.acceptance: Differential tests prove equivalence; benchmark evidence includes branch predictability, vectorization and side-channel constraints.
rules.interpretation_adjustment: Do not automatically replace every conditional with a mask; inspect target/workload effects.

rules.title: Endianness as target property
rules.requirement: Honor the declared target, ABI, device and file-format byte order, with explicit conversion at boundaries.
rules.acceptance: Big- and little-endian fixtures decode correctly; mixed-endian device fields are explicitly documented.
rules.interpretation_adjustment: Do not require Little-Endian globally.

rules.title: Variable-length instruction decoding
rules.requirement: Decode instruction boundaries using the target ISA specification and machine-mode state.
rules.acceptance: Golden byte streams validate length, alignment, prefixes and malformed encoding behavior.
rules.interpretation_adjustment: Do not ban variable-length instruction sets; fixed-width rules apply only to the selected ISA.

rules.title: NOP and alignment planning
rules.requirement: Insert NOP/alignment padding only when required by ISA, ABI, errata, timing or explicit layout constraints.
rules.acceptance: The map file records every inserted NOP and its reason; generated output passes functional and timing tests.
rules.interpretation_adjustment: Do not insert NOPs automatically merely to fill cache-line boundaries.

rules.title: Undefined and reserved instruction handling
rules.requirement: Represent invalid, reserved, unsupported and implementation-defined encodings distinctly in assemblers, decoders and simulators.
rules.acceptance: Negative fixtures verify architectural exception/diagnostic behavior without silently assigning invented semantics.

rules.title: Target-width address model
rules.requirement: Derive virtual/physical address widths, canonical forms and sign-extension rules from the selected ISA/MMU profile.
rules.acceptance: Boundary fixtures reject noncanonical/out-of-range addresses and never silently ignore high bits.
rules.interpretation_adjustment: Do not force 64-bit virtual addresses on 32-bit targets.

rules.title: Page permission and W^X policy
rules.requirement: Represent read/write/execute and device permissions per page/region and enforce W^X where supported by target policy.
rules.acceptance: Negative tests prove disallowed W+X mappings are rejected; deliberate exceptions require an explicit reviewed policy.

rules.title: DMA and IOMMU ownership
rules.requirement: Track device ownership, DMA direction, mapping, pinning, lifetime, IOMMU domain and cache synchronization.
rules.acceptance: State-machine tests reject use-after-unmap, out-of-range descriptor and CPU/device concurrent ownership violations.

rules.title: Out-of-order and retirement model
rules.requirement: Model OoO issue, reorder buffers, speculation, precise retirement and architectural program-order visibility when the selected core supports them.
rules.acceptance: Deterministic traces distinguish issue/execute/retire order and validate architectural state against a reference model.
rules.interpretation_adjustment: Do not assume all CPUs are OoO; in-order cores have separate profiles.

rules.title: Speculative execution and side-channel analysis
rules.requirement: Analyze speculative/transient execution and observable cache/timing channels with target-specific mitigations and test cases.
rules.acceptance: Reports identify known attack surface and mitigation status; no blanket guarantee of eliminating all side channels is made.

rules.title: Power gating and idle-state model
rules.requirement: Describe supported clock/power domains, idle states, gating dependencies and approved control hooks for the target.
rules.acceptance: A model validates sequencing and safety interlocks; physical control requires an exact board/vendor backend and capability.
rules.interpretation_adjustment: Power-gating is not a portable software write to arbitrary transistors.

rules.title: Cycle-accurate simulator qualification
rules.requirement: Provide cycle-accurate simulation only for fully declared microarchitecture models with validated timing inputs.
rules.acceptance: Golden traces match the declared model and reference tests; real silicon correlation reports measured deviation and uncertainty.
rules.interpretation_adjustment: Do not promise exact cycle matching for undocumented commercial silicon.

rules.title: Bounded instruction trace recording
rules.requirement: Record instruction/event traces into a bounded ring buffer with trigger, wrap, loss, sampling and privacy policy.
rules.acceptance: Overflow and dropped events are explicit; trace overhead and perturbation are measured.

rules.title: Fault injection and safety modes
rules.requirement: Inject bit flips, timing faults and device errors in simulation by default; physical fault injection is a separately approved lab mode.
rules.acceptance: Every injection is reproducible and bounded; live injection requires isolation, operator approval and safe-stop procedure.

rules.title: Kernel and driver separation
rules.requirement: Model kernel responsibilities, user-mode services, driver privilege and hardware mediation according to the selected OS.
rules.acceptance: Architecture docs and tests show which components execute in user/kernel/firmware context; no IDE process silently elevates.
rules.interpretation_adjustment: Do not dictate a universal minimal-kernel architecture for all target OSes.

rules.title: Hard real-time evidence gate
rules.requirement: Support deadline analysis, WCET budgets, interrupt load, jitter, scheduling and platform qualification for hard real-time targets.
rules.acceptance: A guarantee is issued only for a named platform/workload with schedulability analysis and HIL evidence; otherwise label estimate or best effort.

rules.title: Virtualization and zero-copy observability
rules.requirement: Expose hardware-assisted virtualization, mappings, exits, IOMMU and data-copy paths for supported hosts/targets.
rules.acceptance: Metrics show actual copies, mappings and exits; overhead is benchmarked, not assumed zero.

rules.title: Hardware breakpoint management
rules.requirement: Manage target-supported hardware breakpoint/watchpoint slots, scope, alignment and debugger side effects.
rules.acceptance: UI reports slot availability and impact; breakpoints beyond capacity fail with a target-specific diagnostic.

rules.title: Logic analyzer and waveform integration
rules.requirement: Show simulator waveforms and optionally ingest physical logic-analyzer/oscilloscope streams through named adapters.
rules.acceptance: Signal names, probe points, sample rates, trigger configuration and calibration/provenance are retained.

rules.title: Live register watch and debug transport
rules.requirement: Support target-appropriate JTAG/SWD/debug providers with explicit halt, sampling, side effects and access permissions.
rules.acceptance: The IDE warns when observation halts or perturbs the target and records transport/session state.

rules.title: Hardware versus model discrepancy workflow
rules.requirement: Compare simulator, architectural specification, errata and live hardware observations and record reproducible divergence.
rules.acceptance: A mismatch is triaged with exact silicon stepping, test, trace and source; observed behavior is not automatically treated as intended architectural behavior.

rules.title: Begin Iron session bootstrap
rules.requirement: Initialize a project session with target profile, toolchain, safety mode, resource budget and provenance before any command runs.
rules.acceptance: A session is ready only after required target/toolchain validation; default operations are inspect/plan/simulate and physical actions remain capability-gated.
rules.interpretation_adjustment: The marker expresses project/session initialization, not an authority to mutate hardware.

implementation_layers.name: Target/session foundation
implementation_layers.gate: A project opens with a validated target identity, mode and evidence context.

implementation_layers.name: Source, IR and machine inspection
implementation_layers.gate: Source/IR/ASM/bytes/register navigation preserves symbol and source provenance.

implementation_layers.name: Memory, device and privilege
implementation_layers.gate: Address, permission, MMIO and device state are explicit and capability-gated.

implementation_layers.name: Simulator and microarchitecture
implementation_layers.gate: Named reference CPU models execute deterministic fixtures and emit synchronized traces.

implementation_layers.name: Debug, trace and replay
implementation_layers.gate: Bounded snapshots, breakpoints, before/after diffs and reproducible simulator replay pass tests.

implementation_layers.name: Timing, power and signal labs
implementation_layers.gate: Measured/estimated/simulated evidence has units, provenance and uncertainty.

implementation_layers.name: HDL, physical design and lab integration
implementation_layers.gate: RTL/EDA/lab adapters pass external tool and physical qualification; research claims remain scoped.

implementation_layers.name: Release and ecosystem maturity
implementation_layers.gate: Windows/Linux builds, target matrix, compatibility migrations and independent qualification pass.

integration_workstreams.title: Deterministic Reaper processor control plane
integration_workstreams.relation: Logical state transitions, plans and replay contracts; not kernel scheduler control.

integration_workstreams.title: Reaper Processor Intelligence
integration_workstreams.relation: Pinned Reaper policy fixtures and report bridge; fixture data is not live hardware telemetry.

integration_workstreams.title: Processor policy and native C11 engine
integration_workstreams.relation: Read-only topology/evidence, affinity-constrained work planning and admission contracts.

integration_workstreams.title: Explicit silicon runtime primitives
integration_workstreams.relation: ISA barriers/cycle sources/MMIO-region concepts; reconcile against main low-level target contract.

integration_workstreams.title: Bounded thread fault recovery
integration_workstreams.relation: Failure correlation and bounded recovery plans.

integration_workstreams.title: Embedded silicon runtime
integration_workstreams.relation: Board HAL/cycle/MMIO callback model; reconcile overlap with #285.

integration_workstreams.title: Processor platform evidence adapters
integration_workstreams.relation: Stacked on #286; read-only WHEA/EDAC evidence and calling-thread affinity lease.

integration_workstreams.title: Processor engineering report
integration_workstreams.relation: Versioned evidence/report envelope; JSON validity is not hardware certification.

integration_workstreams.title: 66-profile processor language workbench
integration_workstreams.relation: Profile registry and inert build planning, not 66 bundled compilers.

safety_adjustments: Assembly-first means deep machine visibility, not a prohibition on Reaper, C, HDL or other explicit source layers.
Sub-nanosecond bus events may be captured by hardware instrumentation; IDE rendering latency is a separate metric and cannot be promised universally.
Endianness, register names, address width, instruction length, cache geometry and privilege levels are target properties, not global constants.
Required stalls, synchronization, speculation barriers and interrupt events cannot be removed for visual neatness.
Physical target writes, fault injection, power gating and debug register writes require named target capabilities and explicit operator approval.

Session flags are declarative preflight metadata only; they never grant hardware access. Actual memory/MMIO/device operations must pass pl_ll_bus capability checks and trusted OS/board backend authorization.
